mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP (more than 1% quarter-over-quarter) indicates a weakening economy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 drops and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over three months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS drops and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within the same month, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending are expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k & UNRATE drops > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% month-over-month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals a weakening demand in the housing sector coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with housing sector weakness
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of HOUST decline and FEDFUNDS level on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
